Subject: FY29 planning: hypotheses, guardrails, and decision horizon

Team — launching FY29 planning thread. Goal: align leadership on the earliest set of planning hypotheses, guardrails for target setting, and a clear decision horizon so product/eng/GT M can start sizing work and hiring asks. High-level asks: 1) propose three scenario bands (base / upside / downside) with clear trigger criteria; 2) surface any structural changes that would alter capacity/cost (e.g., Dedicated vs Private demand); 3) identify program-level hires we must fund to make upside plausible.

Timeline I’m targeting: initial leadership alignment and hypothesis set today (June 1), org-level targets by June 8, finance-ready request package June 15. If you see blockers to that cadence call it out now.

I uploaded a lightweight template and a working hypothesis workbook to the planning Drive folder (link below). Please drop one-line red flags and owners against each item in the doc by EOD Tuesday. We’ll run a 30-minute check-in at 2pm PT to triage open items and lock owners.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d-planning-fy29

Initial framing:
- Base: modest growth, maintains current GTM efficiency; hires limited to critical infra and customer success coverage.
- Upside: step-change adoption from a major marketplace partner + one enterprise expansion; funds selective hiring for platform and solutions engineering.
- Downside: macro slowdown reduces new logos and delays Dedicated deals; prioritize cost flexibility and runway.

Please review the attached planning_hypotheses_v1 for my initial assumptions. I expect edits — treat this as a starting point.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Finance & Strategy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FY29 planning: hypotheses, guardrails, and decision horizon

Thanks Kim — I pushed a first pass at a scenario matrix to the folder (scenario_matrix_v1.csv) and attached a short vendor impact note. Key points from my pass:
- Revenue drivers: Hosted API adoption (lower friction, higher churn risk), Dedicated bookings (lumpy, high ACV), Partners (predictable but long lead).
- Capacity assumptions: Upside assumes 25% higher average sequence length and 15% more concurrent sessions; base is +8% over run-rate. We should model cost-per-token under two quantization profiles to see sensitivity.
- Hiring: to hit upside defensibly we need 6 FTEs (2 infra, 2 platform eng, 2 solutions/AE) phased across H1/H2. If we’re tight, recommend prioritizing Platform Eng over AE in H1.

Attachments: scenario_matrix_v1.csv (scenario rows + triggers), vendor_impact_note.txt (short list). I flagged a procurement timeline question for Caspian Analytics — their procurement lead wants SOC 2 evidence and a 45-day procurement window for Dedicated deals (cc’d procurement@caspiananalytics.com).

Jonas Weber
Director, GTM Strategy

- Procurement timing: confirm SOC 2 artifact list and estimated procurement windows for top 3 pilot accounts (Marissa, by June 8).
- Hiring prioritization: draft a phased hiring plan aligned to revenue triggers (Vivek + Talent, by June 8).
- Finance package: assemble the finance request packet for June 15 submission (Kimberly + Lauren).

Meeting: 2:00pm PT / 30m (Calendar invite sent).

If any of these owners are overloaded ping me and I will reassign. I also added a short checklist for QBR narrative—please add one-line talking points for your area before Friday.
